title: Ajamila calls his son
hookLine: a name read wrong at rehearsal, a dying man calling his son, and why so many Hindu children carry a god's name
carry: god's name reaches god, even called to a child
tomorrow: how can a puff of air on your palm change a whole word?

lines: IT MATTERS MORE THAN YOU KNOW.
cards: Roll call on the first day of anything. A name gets read off the list, and it comes out squashed, or stretched in the wrong places. Some people correct it every time.
Some give up and answer to the wrong name for years. It can feel small and still sting. Hindu tradition says a name can matter more than anyone in the room knows.

teach.b: In the Bhagavata Purana, a man named Ajamila had thrown away nearly everything good in his life. He cheated, he stole, he left the family that loved him.

But he adored his youngest son, a little boy named Narayana, one of the names of Vishnu. At eighty-eight, Ajamila lay dying, and he saw three fierce figures come for him with ropes: the messengers of Yama, lord of death.
Terrified, he cried out for his boy. Narayana! At once, messengers of Vishnu appeared and stopped Yama's.
He has said the Lord's name, they said. Even called out for a child, the name has done its work. Ajamila lived, and gave the rest of his life to devotion.
The Bhagavata draws the lesson itself: God's name, said even in passing, even meaning something else, still reaches God.
That's one reason so many Hindu children are named for gods: Krishna, Lakshmi, Ganesh, Durga, Shiva. Many families say it plainly: every time you call your child, you've said God's name.

teach.h: A NAME CAN BE A PRAYER.
teach.b: A name chosen at the namakarana, the naming rite, can be a prayer said a dozen times a day without anyone noticing. So a name isn't only a label. Said with care, it may be the most repeated prayer in the house.

how: Many Hindu families choose a god's name, or a name for one of a god's qualities, at the namakarana, the naming rite held in the days after birth, so the child is called by a holy name every day.

games.q: at a cousin's naming ceremony, a friend asks why the baby gets a god's name, Ganesh, when everyone will just call him Ganu. what's a good answer?
o: every time they call him, they say God's name; Ajamila's story says that counts.
parents pick gods' names so the baby will be well-known.
games.why: in the Bhagavata, Ajamila called his son Narayana and the name reached God anyway. many families choose gods' names so the holy name is said every day.

practice: Say your own name slowly, and if you know what it means, let the meaning sit with it. Then say the name of someone you love, with care, as a small blessing.
If you pray, end with one name of God, said the way Ajamila said it: as a call. Then rest with the breath.
